judgements.justification: Both committees gave 8, 7, 7, 6; B's area chair cited only 'sufficient positive feedback and support' for a spotlight and A's gave a poster on the same profile, so the split sits in the tier threshold.
A's best-informed reviewer, Reviewer_skXW, gave an accept 8; A's meta-review answers his concurrent-work point directly, so his verdict was weighed, not passed over.
No score moved in either committee after the response; neither committee's concerns were lifted by the rebuttal more than the other's.
Neither committee has an outlier; all ratings lie within one point of the shared 7.0 mean.
No outlying reviewer exists in either committee.
Neither committee had a low-scoring detractor; the lowest score in each is a 6 and no area chair defended acceptance against one.
Reviewer_skXW called explainable clustering 'an artificial problem' but still gave 8; no reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit.
B's meta-review accurately reports reviewer support, and A's accurately answers Reviewer_skXW; neither misstates positions or the rebuttal.
A's reviewers did not reply, but B's reviewers did not revise either (Reviewer_fBhF replied yet kept 7), so no engaged-and-revised contrast exists.
No reviewer in either committee said they could not verify the results; confidences are 4 except B's Reviewer_gBnK at 3 after a 10-hour review.
Neither committee split between accept and reject; all scores are 6 to 8.
The responses address different questions (the Eq. (1) typo in B, independence of the ICML papers in A) but do not conflict in substance.
The overlooked Makarychev and Shan paper is concurrent, not prior, work, and both area chairs treated it as independent; no novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work.
B's spotlight has no stated grounds: no B reviewer argued for a highlight and the meta-review gives only 'sufficient positive feedback and support' on a 7.0 mean.
No reviewer objected to the framing from a neighbouring field's premises; Reviewer_skXW's 'artificial problem' remark is an in-field judgement that did not lower his 8.
Neither committee had a reviewer well above the accept level arguing against critics; each top score is an 8, and B's is a thin four-sentence review.
No reviewer or area chair judged promised revisions too large for camera-ready.
Both area chairs worked from the visible reviews; B's area chair raised the concurrent overlap itself but used it only to ask for a related-work update.
A's reviewers (Reviewer_tp15, Reviewer_X5Zn, Reviewer_Hp5d) kept missing experiments as a standing reservation on a theory paper, while B's Reviewer_fBhF accepted that a theory paper needs none.
No score fell below the accept threshold; the 6s in each committee rest on general reservations, not a peripheral point held after the rebuttal.
